unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 5: Securities and modes of charge I — Identify the secured obligation, specific immovable property and transferred interest without equating every security with a mortgage

facts.statement: Courseware introduces security/charge in lending and section 58(a) mortgage definitions, including money to be advanced, future debt and pecuniary liability.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 188; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Section 58(a) defines a mortgage as transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the stated secured monetary purposes, with mortgagor/mortgagee/mortgage-money/deed terminology. Section 100 concerns immovable property made security where the transaction does not amount to a mortgage; the general banking use of charge is broader than this statutory distinction.
facts.locator: sections 58(a) and 100, official Delhi text headings

payload.title: Build a security file around the obligation and the property
payload.core_explanation_md:
For a mortgage analysis, identify **whose interest is being offered, which specific immovable property it concerns, and what obligation it secures**. Section 58(a) is not limited to a loan already disbursed. It also addresses money to be advanced, existing or future debt and an engagement that may create a monetary liability.

The person transferring the interest is the **mortgagor**; the recipient is the **mortgagee**. The secured principal and interest are the mortgage-money. The instrument, if any, effecting the transfer is the mortgage-deed. These roles should be traced to the documents rather than assumed from who visits the branch.

An outright sale for an independent purchase price and a transfer structured to secure a debt have different purposes. Inspect the operative arrangement; a document label or the word security alone does not finish the classification.

self_check.prompt_text: Must the advance already have been disbursed for section 58(a) to be relevant?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The definition includes money to be advanced and the stated future-debt or monetary-liability purposes.

payload.title: Separate the lending shorthand from the statutory category
payload.core_explanation_md:
Banking files often use **charge** broadly for a security interest. Section 100 uses a more particular immovable-property category: property is made security for payment, but the transaction does **not amount to a mortgage**. That statutory distinction should be preserved when a question asks which legal arrangement was created.

Do not infer a mortgage merely because a sanction letter calls something collateral. Equally, do not treat every reference to a charge as proof that no mortgage exists. The underlying transaction, property and transfer of interest must be examined. A valid secured transaction also needs the applicable formalities and authority; classification is not a substitute for those checks.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the word charge in a sanction letter insufficient to settle the statutory classification?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The underlying transaction may be a mortgage or another security arrangement; section 100 has a specific scope.

payload.stem_md: A bank proposes property security for an undrawn facility. A reviewer rejects mortgage analysis solely because no money has yet been disbursed. Which point in section 58(a) needs attention?

options.text_md: A mortgage can secure only principal already paid out
options.explanation_md: The definition expressly extends beyond money already advanced.

options.text_md: The definition can cover money to be advanced and the stated future monetary obligations
options.explanation_md: An undrawn facility is not excluded solely by the absence of an earlier disbursement; the remaining creation requirements still need examination.

options.text_md: Any proposed future facility automatically transfers ownership without documents
options.explanation_md: The future-advance purpose does not itself create a valid mortgage or remove its formalities.

options.text_md: Future obligations can be secured only by movable assets
options.explanation_md: Section 58(a) expressly concerns the stated purposes secured through specific immovable property.

payload.correct_explanation_md: An undrawn facility is not excluded solely by the absence of an earlier disbursement; the remaining creation requirements still need examination.

payload.stem_md: A legal note distinguishes an immovable-property charge under section 100 from a mortgage. Which fact is central to that distinction?

options.text_md: Whether the lender calls the property collateral
options.explanation_md: Commercial terminology alone does not decide which statutory security arrangement exists.

options.text_md: Whether the borrower has already defaulted
options.explanation_md: Default affects remedies; it does not alone determine whether the transaction amounted to a mortgage at creation.

options.text_md: Whether interest is payable on the underlying loan
options.explanation_md: Interest alone is not the distinction between section 100 security and a mortgage.

options.text_md: Whether the transaction amounts to a mortgage rather than merely making the property security for payment
options.explanation_md: Section 100 expressly addresses security that does not amount to a mortgage; the operative transaction must be examined.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 100 expressly addresses security that does not amount to a mortgage; the operative transaction must be examined.
